heading: INT. GRAND HOTEL LIBRARY, MONTE VERDE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. GRAND HOTEL LIBRARY, MONTE VERDE - NIGHT
Leather armchairs.
A fire in a marble hearth.
A ladder on a brass rail.
Rain on tall windows.
A decanter on a silver tray.
LADY ISABELLA CORVINO-HARTWELL (50s, emerald silk, a cigarette holder) pours two glasses of brandy.
Across the room, MR. CORNELIUS BANKOLE-FAIRWEATHER (60s, tuxedo, white gloves) examines a leatherbound volume.
And by the fire, DR. ANNELIESE VOSSBERG-KANE (40s, plain gray dress, a doctor's bag at her feet) warms her hands.
Cornelius, you'll tire your eyes.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: My eyes have survived worse than Boccaccio.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: Anneliese, you must be cold.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: I am quite well, Lady Corvino.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Isabella carries a glass across the room and hands it to the doctor.
Anneliese accepts it, sniffs it, and does not drink.
You don't care for brandy?
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: I care for knowing what's in it.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: A pause.
The fire pops.
Cornelius shuts his book.
Bella, our guest is being cautious.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: Our guest is being rude.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: Our guest is a physician. I've examined enough of your late husband's guests to know the habits of this house.
units.name: ANNELIESE
paren: setting the glass on the mantel

units.text: How dreadfully dramatic.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: He died on this carpet, Lady Corvino. Not in his bed.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Dr. Vossberg--
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: ^Anneliese--
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: They speak together, stop, glare at one another.
Anneliese lifts her bag onto the sofa and opens it.
I've brought what's left of his glass. The one you didn't wash.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Isabella's cigarette holder trembles.
Cornelius takes one step toward the doctor, then thinks better of it.
You have no proof.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: I have a vial. And a friend at the laboratory in Geneva who owes me a favor.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: What do you want?
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: I want to know who poured the first glass.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Silence.
Rain.
Isabella walks to the window.
Her reflection stares back, thin and white.
Cornelius studies the floor.
Anneliese closes the bag, snaps it shut.
It was never meant for him.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: Then who?
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Isabella turns.
She looks, not at the doctor, but at Cornelius.
He does not look up.
His gloved hands close slowly into fists.
Bella.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: You told me it was a sleeping draught.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: It was.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: For him.
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: For him.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: Then why is the doctor here?
units.name: ISABELLA

units.text: Because she was always going to be here.
units.name: CORNELIUS

units.text: He lifts his eyes to Anneliese, and there is nothing in them but a long, tired courtesy.
Mr. Bankole-Fairweather. Pour yourself a brandy.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: He crosses to the decanter.
Pours with perfect steadiness.
Raises the glass.
Looks at the fire.
Drinks.
The glass slips from his hand and shatters on the marble.
I told you. I care about what's in it.
units.name: ANNELIESE

units.text: Isabella sinks into an armchair.
The fire cracks.
A discreet knock.
BUTLER AUGUSTUS PELLEGRINI-OSEI (60s, immaculate, expressionless) enters with a fresh log, sees the shards, sees the body, and sets the log down very gently.
Shall I send for the constable, my lady, or for the undertaker?
units.name: AUGUSTUS

units.text: Both, Augustus. In that order.
units.name: ISABELLA
